questions.q_en: If height of a trapezium is 30 cm and sum of the parallel sides of the trapezium is equal to the area of square whose side is 13 cm. find the area of the trapezium.
questions.solution_en:
Area of square = 13 * 13 = 169 cm2

Distance = 30 cm

Area of trapezium = 1/2 * (sum of parallel sides) * distance between them

=> 1/2 * 169 * 30 = 2535 cm2

For cone => Radius = 5 cm, height = 6 cm

For cylinder => Radius = 2.5 cm, height = 3 cm

Ratio = (volume of cone/volume of cylinder)

= (1/3 * π * 52 * 6)/ (π * 2.52 * 3)

= (4*2)/3

questions.q_en: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 hours and 25 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 5 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.solution_en:
Work done by Pipe A in 1 hour = 1 / 15

Work done by Pipe B in 1 hour = 1 / 25

Work done by Pipe C in 1 hour = -1 / 40 (negative because it empties the tank)

Total work done in 1 hour by all three pipes:

(1 / 15) + (1 / 25) - (1 / 40)

LCM of 15, 25, and 40 = 600

Total work = (40 / 600) + (24 / 600) - (15 / 600) = (40 + 24 - 15) / 600 = 49 / 600

Work done in 1 hour = 49 / 600

Total work in 5 hours = 5 X (49 / 600) = 245 / 600

Fraction of tank filled in 5 hours = 245 / 600

Remaining part of the tank = 1 - (245 / 600) = (600 - 245) / 600 = 355 / 600

Work done by Pipe B and Pipe C in 1 hour (after Pipe A is closed):

Work done by Pipe B in 1 hour = 1 / 25

Work done by Pipe C in 1 hour = -1 / 40

Total work done in 1 hour by Pipe B and Pipe C:

(1 / 25) - (1 / 40)

LCM of 25 and 40 = 200

Total work = (8 / 200) - (5 / 200) = 3 / 200

Work done in 1 hour = 3 / 200

Remaining work = 355 / 600

Time = Remaining work / Work done in 1 hour

Time = (355 / 600) / (3 / 200)

Time = (355 X 200) / (600 X 3) = 71000 / 1800 = 355/9 or 39(4/9) hours

questions.q_en: Three positive numbers A, B, and C are co-prime to each other. If product of A and B is 399 and product of B and C is 840 then, the value of A + B - C is:
questions.solution_en:
A * B = 399

B * C = 840

(A * B)/ (B * C) = 399/840

A/C = 19/40

Since A, B, and C are co - prime so, A = 19 and C = 40

And B = 21

Now, value of A + B - C = 19 + 21 - 40 = 40 - 40 = 0

questions.q_en: Rakesh gives a discount of 20% and thus makes a profit of 20%. If due to increase in transportation cost the cost price of his item increases by 15% then what should be the discount percentage in this case if list price remains unchanged and Rakesh wants to retain same profit percentage?
questions.solution_en:
Let the Cost price = Rs 100a

Hence selling Price with 20% profit = Rs (100a X 1.2) = Rs 120a

Marked price with 20% discount = 120 x 100/80 = Rs 150a

Now cost price increased by 15%.

So, new CP = Rs 100 x 1.15 = Rs 115a

Selling price of the item to make a profit of 20% = Rs (115a X 1.2) = Rs 138a

Required discount percentage = (150-138)/150 x 100 = 8%

questions.q_en: Which is the largest six-digit number, which when divided by 12,15, 20, 24 and 30, leaves the remainders 8, 11, 16, 20 and 26, respectively.
questions.solution_en:
The LCM of 12, 15 20,24, 30 = 120

the greatest of 6-digit = 999999

Dividing 999999 by 120 we get 39 as the remainder

Hence the 6-digit number divisible by 120 is (999999-39)

= 999960

Since 12-8=4, 15-11 = 4, 20-16=4, 24-20= 4, 30-26 = 4

then reminder is each case is =4 less than the divisor

Hence, Required number = 999960-4 = 999956

questions.q_en: The average weight of a class of 10 students is increased by 2 kg when one student of 30 kg left and another student joined. After a few months, new student left and another student joined whose weight was 10 less than the students who left now. What is the difference between the final and initial average?
questions.solution_en:
"

Change is total weight of 10 students  = Difference in weight of the student who joined and left 

Weight of first student who left = 30 + (10 × 2) =  50 kg. 

Weight of the students who joined last = 50 –10 = 40 kg

So, change in average weight =    = 1 kg

"

questions.q_en: A has a sum of ₹450 and he wants to pay the sum to B by using coins of ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10. He uses a total of 109 coins. If the ratio of ₹2 and ₹5 coins used is 5:8, then how many coins of ₹10 are used in the payment?
questions.solution_en:
Total number of coins of ₹2 and ₹5 are 5n and 8n respectively.

Total number of coins of ₹10 = 109 - 5n - 8n = 109 - 13n

Now,

2*5n + 5*8n + 10*(109 - 13n) = 450

10n + 40n + 1090 - 130n = 450

80n = 640

n = 8

Total number of coins of ₹10 are used in the payment = 109 - 13*8 = 5

questions.q_en: If a cube is melted and converted in to 1000 cubes of equal volumes, then total surface area of a smaller cube is how much percent less than the total surface area of bigger cube?
questions.solution_en:
Let the side of cube be A

Total surface area = 6 x A2

Volume = A3

Volume of each small cube = (A3/1000)

Side of each small cube = (A/10)

Total surface area of each small cube = 6 (A/10)2 = 6(A2/100)

Required percentage change = 100% - (((6(A2/100))/ (6 x A2)) x 100%) = 100% - 1% = 99%.

Pipe A and pipe B together can fill the tank in 16 hours. Pipe B and pipe C together can fill the tank in 32 hours. Pipe C and pipe A together can fill the tank in 48 hours. Find the time taken by pipes A, B, and C to fill the tank.
questions.solution_en:
The capacity of tank = L.C.M of 16, 32, and 48 = 96

Efficiency = total capacity/ time taken

Efficiency of pipes A and B = 96/16 = 6

Efficiency of pipes B and C = 96/32 = 3

Efficiency of pipes C and A = 96/48 = 2

Efficiency of pipes A, B, and C = (6 + 3 + 2)/2 = 11/2

The required time = 96/ (11/2) = 192/11 hours
